_readme: CONTRACT STRINGS. The English text in options[].text, limitationRules[].limitation / whenAcuity and questions[].scoreEffects[].whenAnswer / filters[].unlessAnswerContains IS the stored survey answer AND the rule-matching key. Rewording any of them without updating every rule that names it silently disables exclusion/scoring. This file MUST stay byte-identical between Rise/Rise/Resources/Mappings/exercise_recommender_v1.json and Rise-android/app/src/main/assets/exercise_recommender_v1.json (checksum-pinned by PhysicalAbilitiesGateWiringTests / PhysicalAbilitiesGateWiringTest). Every taskKey named anywhere in this file must exist in baseHabitTasksMap on BOTH platforms. NO OPTION TEXT MAY CONTAIN ', ' — multi-select answers are stored as a ', '-joined string, so a comma inside one option splits it into two phantom segments and every rule that names it stops matching. COPY IS HEALTH-ADJACENT: describe the ACTIVITY ('low-impact'), never assert an outcome about the user's named condition ('zero impact on it', 'safe for your knee'). Absolutes are falsified by one counterexample — walking is low-impact but fully weight-bearing. Each rule's `axis` selects the template: impact framing applies to musculoskeletal only; cardiorespiratory gets the talk test, perinatal defers to a clinician, musculoskeletal_acute defers to a clinician AND drops every loaded option. TRANSLATOR NOTE: 'low-impact' means little force/shock through the joints, NOT low effort.
_clinicalReadme: ACUITY IS A SAFETY DIMENSION, NOT A PREFERENCE. Injury SITE (knee vs ankle vs hip/leg vs back vs shoulder) and injury AGE (new / healing / long-term) load differently, so they are asked separately and each rule carries the source it was written from in `citation`. Rules are FAIL-SAFE BY CONSTRUCTION: every musculoskeletal site has a BASE rule with no `whenAcuity`, so an unanswered or unrecognised acuity answer still applies the conservative baseline — an acuity-gated rule only ever ADDS exclusions on top (exclusions union across all matching rules). NEVER convert a base rule into an acuity-gated one. Rules are ordered acute → healing → base → non-musculoskeletal because `firstMatchingRule` (JSON order) picks the copy the screen speaks with, and the acute case must win. Where the cited guidance does not clearly support recommending an activity for a stated condition, the rule EXCLUDES it rather than substituting a safer-sounding one. Any edit to limitationRules is health-adjacent content and needs human sign-off before it ships — see docs/dev/physical-abilities-clinical-basis.md.

limitationRules.citation: Mayo Clinic 'Sprained ankle' — severe-sprain symptoms resemble a broken bone and need prompt evaluation; AAOS 'Sprained Ankle' — seek assessment where weight-bearing is difficult. An undifferentiated NEW injury is not something to prescribe loaded exercise for, so every loaded option is excluded and the copy defers to a clinician. NHS back-pain and NHS/CUH acute-ankle guidance both support staying gently active rather than resting completely, which is why walking and gentle floor work remain.

AAOS 'Sprained Ankle' + Mayo Clinic 'Ankle pain — when to see a doctor': difficulty bearing weight or bony tenderness needs evaluation to rule out fracture. NHS/CUH acute-ankle advice supports early weight-bearing and gentle movement, so walking and gentle floor work stay while every loaded or equipment-based option is excluded.

Same basis as the acute knee and ankle rules — an undifferentiated new lower-limb injury is not safely distinguishable from a fracture in a survey, so no loaded activity is recommended and the copy defers to a clinician (Mayo Clinic sprain first aid; AAOS).

NHS 'Back pain' — staying active aids recovery and bed rest is NOT recommended, gentle exercise is advised in the early stages, and users are told to stop and see a GP if pain worsens. Walking and gentle floor work are therefore kept; loaded, twisting and impact options are excluded until it settles.

AAOS 'Shoulder Impingement / Rotator Cuff Tendinitis' — rest and activity modification, avoiding the overhead activity that provokes symptoms; AAOS rotator-cuff rehab guidance advises using pain as the guide and stopping painful exercise. Lower-body walking is unaffected by the shoulder and is kept.

whenAcuity: It's healing but not back to normal
limitationRules.citation: NHS Royal National Orthopaedic Hospital knee rehab: rehabilitation should be built up GRADUALLY with a graduated increase in difficulty. Low-load options (swimming, cycling, walking) are retained per AAOS 'Arthritis of the Knee' and Versus Arthritis; high-impact, cutting and heavy-load work stays out until it is back to normal.

whenAcuity: It's healing but not back to normal
limitationRules.citation: AAOS 'Sprained Ankle' — rehabilitation restores flexibility, strength and proprioception before return to sport, and minor sprains take ~2 weeks while severe ones take 6-12. Uneven-ground and cutting sports stay excluded during that window; swimming and walking lead the replacements.

whenAcuity: It's healing but not back to normal
limitationRules.citation: Graduated-return principle as per NHS orthopaedic rehab guidance; low-load aerobic options (swimming, walking, cycling) retained per AAOS 'Managing Arthritis Pain With Exercise' as the standard alternatives to high-impact activity.

whenAcuity: It's healing but not back to normal
limitationRules.citation: NHS 'Back pain' — walking, swimming, yoga and pilates all have broadly similar benefit and staying active aids recovery. Heavy axial loading and impact sport stay out while it is still settling.

whenAcuity: It's healing but not back to normal
limitationRules.citation: AAOS rotator-cuff conditioning guidance — graduated return, pain as the guide, avoid the provoking overhead load. Lower-body aerobic work is unaffected and leads the replacements.

AAOS 'Arthritis of the Knee' and Versus Arthritis 'Osteoarthritis of the knee' — walking, swimming and cycling are the recommended lower-load alternatives to running and competitive sport; NHS knee-OA physiotherapy guidance lists cycling and swimming as load-reducing. BASE RULE: applies at every acuity including unanswered, so it must stay conservative.

AAOS 'Sprained Ankle' — repeated sprains follow returning to cutting and uneven-ground activity; hiking is excluded here (and NOT in the knee rule) precisely because the ankle bucket was previously collapsed into the knee one. BASE RULE: applies at every acuity including unanswered.

AAOS 'Managing Arthritis Pain With Exercise' — low-impact aerobic activity (walking, swimming, cycling) in place of high-impact and competitive sport. BASE RULE: applies at every acuity including unanswered.

NHS 'Back pain' — walking, running, cycling, SWIMMING, yoga and pilates all have similar effects and swimming takes strain off joints and muscles. This is why swim is a REPLACEMENT here and not an exclusion; the previous collapsed 'Back or shoulder problem' bucket excluded swimming from back-pain users against NHS advice. Heavy axial loading and impact/twisting sport remain excluded. BASE RULE: applies at every acuity including unanswered.

AAOS 'Shoulder Impingement / Rotator Cuff Tendinitis' and 'Common Shoulder Injuries' — shoulder injury is frequently caused by repetitive OVERHEAD motion, naming swimming, tennis, pitching and weightlifting; treatment is rest and avoiding overhead activity. This is why swim IS excluded here while it is recommended for back problems — the two were previously one bucket with one answer. BASE RULE: applies at every acuity including unanswered.

AAOS 'Managing Arthritis Pain With Exercise' and Versus Arthritis 'Osteoarthritis of the knee' — exercises that reduce joint load (swimming, cycling, water-based work) are recommended, and walking/swimming/cycling are the named alternatives to high-impact and competitive sport. Unchanged from v1 apart from re-verification.

The relevant axis is EXERTION, not impact. The talk test is an established marker of the moderate/vigorous boundary and is consistent across walking, cycling and other modes (cardiac-rehabilitation literature); NHS knee-OA guidance phrases the same rule as working hard enough to get out of breath but still able to hold a conversation, which is the wording the copy uses. Unchanged from v1 apart from re-verification.

ACOG 'Exercise During Pregnancy' — brisk walking, swimming and water workouts, modified yoga and modified pilates are the named safe activities; activities with a risk of FALLING or impact to the abdomen should be avoided, explicitly naming off-road cycling and contact sports such as soccer and basketball. CHANGED IN THIS REVISION: cycling added to the exclusions on that basis. Copy defers to the user's own clinician.

No source supports recommending ambulatory or equipment-based exercise to a user who has told us their mobility is limited, so none is recommended — the honest output is seated/floor-based and non-physical options. Unchanged from v1.
